title: Vintage Gibson ES-335 Value Guide: Prices By Year To 1979
description: Vintage Gibson ES-335 values by year, with dot-neck and later price ranges, finish and tailpiece differences, repair guidance and photos from my archive.
alt: Sunburst Gibson ES-335 with dot inlays, two covered pickups and a stopbar in a pink-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson ES-335 Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson ES-335 guide values run from $3,000 to $5,000 for typical 1970s examples to $30,000 to $63,000 for early dot-neck guitars, reviewed in October 2026. The broader all-original dot-neck market spans $27,000 to $72,000+, so the table isn't a ceiling for a rare or exceptional guitar.

faqs.q: Does A Natural Finish Use The Sunburst Range?
faqs.a: No. Original natural-finish early ES-335s are outside the ordinary sunburst and cherry ranges. I appraise those finishes individually.

faqs.q: Why Is The 1968 Figure Different From 1969?
faqs.a: The 1968 row gives a $6,500 to $7,500 range for clean originals. The 1969 row allows played condition and marks the multi-piece neck and shorter tenon transition. Condition and construction both affect the appraisal.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson ES-335 Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in the condition notes. A full refinish changes the collector category, so I assess the finish work, retained parts and repairs individually. The reduction depends on the quality of the work, era and retained original parts.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson ES-335 Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
